title: Ordinal reversal transports extra degeneracies and reverses homotopy endpoints
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category, and use simplicial objects as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] and combinatorial homotopies with the endpoint and prism conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. For an order-preserving map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, set $r(\alpha)(j)=n-\alpha(m-j)$. This defines an involutive functor $r:\Delta\to\Delta$. Write $W^r=W\circ r^{\mathrm{op}}$ for a simplicial object $W$; it has $W^r_n=W_n$, faces $d_i^r=d_{n-i}$ on degree $n$, and degeneracies $s_i^r=s_{n-i}$ on degree $n$. For $q_n:[n]\to[0]$ one has $r(q_n)=q_n$.
Let $p:W\to\operatorname{const}Y$ be an augmentation and suppose maps $t_{-1}:Y\to W_0$, $t_n:W_n\to W_{n+1}$ satisfy
$$p_0t_{-1}=1_Y,\quad d_{n+1}t_n=1_{W_n},\quad d_0t_0=t_{-1}p_0,$$
$$d_it_{n+1}=t_nd_i\quad(0\leq i\leq n+1),\qquad s_it_n=t_{n+1}s_i\quad(0\leq i\leq n),\quad n\geq0.$$
Then the same maps are left extra-degeneracy data for $p^r:W^r\to\operatorname{const}Y$ in exactly the sense of [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. A simplicial section $a^r$ of $p^r$ becomes a section $a$ of $p$ with the same degree components; in particular $W^r(q_n)t_{-1}=W(q_n)t_{-1}$.
More generally, let $A,B$ be simplicial objects in $\mathcal C$, $f,g:A\to B$ simplicial maps, and $H$ a combinatorial homotopy from $f^r$ to $g^r$. Then $\widetilde H_j^n=H_{n-j}^n$ for $0\leq j\leq n$ is a combinatorial homotopy from $g$ to $f$. All these operations commute with natural maps of the supplied diagrams and with evaluation in a parameter functor category.

Returned proof steps 6 and 7: involution of the simplex category, conversion of right to left extra degeneracies, unchanged section, and all endpoint/face/degeneracy identities of the transported prism homotopy.

proof.text: Use the functor definition of simplicial objects in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. If $j\leq k$ then $m-k\leq m-j$, hence $n-\alpha(m-j)\leq n-\alpha(m-k)$, so $r(\alpha)$ is monotone. For $\beta:[n]\to[\ell]$, substitution gives $r(\beta\alpha)(j)=\ell-\beta(\alpha(m-j))=r(\beta)(r(\alpha)(j))$. Also $r(1_{[n]})(j)=j$ and $r(r(\alpha))(j)=\alpha(j)$. Thus $r$ is an involutive functor, and precomposition defines $W^r$ and takes natural transformations to natural transformations.

proof.text: The coface $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ omits $i$. Its reversal is the increasing injection omitting $n-i$, so $r(\delta_i)=\delta_{n-i}$. The codegeneracy $\sigma_i:[n+1]\to[n]$ repeats $i$; its reversal repeats $n-i$, so $r(\sigma_i)=\sigma_{n-i}$. Applying the face and degeneracy definitions of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] proves $d_i^r=d_{n-i}$ and $s_i^r=s_{n-i}$ on degree $n$. Finally $r(q_n)(j)=0-q_n(n-j)=0$, so $r(q_n)=q_n$. Reversal fixes the constant functor and leaves the degree components of every natural transformation unchanged; in particular $p_n^r=p_n$.

source.place: Tag 08ND (lemma-standard-simplicial-homotopy), second homotopy equivalence, in Situation 08N9; explicit agent-written index-reversal calculation supplementing the source. Homotopy and extra-degeneracy conventions: the statement of lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism.

proof.text: Check the left extra-degeneracy equations displayed in [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism] with $Z=W^r$, $e=p^r$, and $h=t$. The augmentation equation is $p_0t_{-1}=1$. Since $t_n$ lands in degree $n+1$, $d_0^rt_n=d_{n+1}t_n=1$, and $d_1^rt_0=d_0t_0=t_{-1}p_0$. For $0\leq i\leq n+1$, put $k=n+1-i$, which lies in the same range. On the two relevant degrees, $d_{i+1}^rt_{n+1}=d_kt_{n+1}=t_nd_k=t_nd_i^r$. These are all the required face equations.

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq n$, put $k=n-i$. The degeneracy on the target of $t_n$ has degree $n+1$, whereas that on its source has degree $n$. Consequently $s_{i+1}^rt_n=s_kt_n=t_{n+1}s_k=t_{n+1}s_i^r$. This gives every degeneracy equation in [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. Together with the preceding step it proves that exactly the supplied maps give left extra-degeneracy data, without imposing any additional relation on the $t_n$.

source.place: Tag 08ND (lemma-standard-simplicial-homotopy), second homotopy equivalence, in Situation 08N9; explicit agent-written index-reversal calculation supplementing the source. Homotopy and extra-degeneracy conventions: the statement of lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism.

proof.text: Let $a^r$ be any simplicial section of $p^r$. For any $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, naturality of $a^r$ at $r(\alpha)$ says $W^r(r(\alpha))a_n^r=a_m^r$. Involution identifies the left operator with $W(\alpha)$, so the same components define a natural transformation $a$ to $W$. The equality $p_na_n=1_Y$ is the unchanged section equality. In particular, the explicit section in [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism] has components $W^r(q_n)t_{-1}=W(r(q_n))t_{-1}=W(q_n)t_{-1}$.

proof.text: For the homotopy calculation, write $D_i,S_i$ for operators on the reversed objects, reserving $d_i,s_i$ for the original objects, and set $k=n-j$. The maps $\widetilde H_j^n=H_k^n$ have the required type $A_n\to B_{n+1}$. The endpoint equations of [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism] give $d_0\widetilde H_0^n=D_{n+1}H_n^n=f_n$ and $d_{n+1}\widetilde H_n^n=D_0H_0^n=g_n$. These are precisely the endpoints for a homotopy from $g$ to $f$ under the stated convention, including when $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 08ND (lemma-standard-simplicial-homotopy), second homotopy equivalence, in Situation 08N9; explicit agent-written index-reversal calculation supplementing the source. Homotopy and extra-degeneracy conventions: the statement of lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism.

proof.text: Check the two strict face cases using the identities in [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. If $i<j$, then $n+1-i>k+1$ and $d_i\widetilde H_j^n=D_{n+1-i}H_k^n=H_k^{n-1}D_{n-i}=\widetilde H_{j-1}^{n-1}d_i$. If $i>j+1$, then $n+1-i<k$ and $d_i\widetilde H_j^n=D_{n+1-i}H_k^n=H_{k-1}^{n-1}D_{n+1-i}=\widetilde H_j^{n-1}d_{i-1}$. These cases require $n\geq1$ and their inequalities ensure the displayed degree-$(n-1)$ homotopy indices exist. For the middle equation, $j<n$ gives $1\leq k\leq n$; the original middle equation at index $k-1$ is $D_kH_k^n=D_kH_{k-1}^n$. Since $d_{j+1}=D_k$ in degree $n+1$, this is $d_{j+1}\widetilde H_{j+1}^n=d_{j+1}\widetilde H_j^n$.

source.place: Tag 08ND (lemma-standard-simplicial-homotopy), second homotopy equivalence, in Situation 08N9; explicit agent-written index-reversal calculation supplementing the source. Homotopy and extra-degeneracy conventions: the statement of lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism.

proof.text: For degeneracies, $s_i\widetilde H_j^n=S_{n+1-i}H_k^n$. If $i\leq j$, then $n+1-i>k$, so the second degeneracy equation in [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism] makes this $H_k^{n+1}S_{n-i}=\widetilde H_{j+1}^{n+1}s_i$. If $i>j$, then $n+1-i\leq k$, so its first degeneracy equation makes this $H_{k+1}^{n+1}S_{n+1-i}=\widetilde H_j^{n+1}s_{i-1}$. Here the $S$ on the right acts on $A_n$, which is why its reversed index is $n$ minus its index. Both formulas hold for the full range $0\leq i\leq n+1$, with the respective inequalities. This verifies every homotopy identity.

source.place: Tag 08ND (lemma-standard-simplicial-homotopy), second homotopy equivalence, in Situation 08N9; explicit agent-written index-reversal calculation supplementing the source. Homotopy and extra-degeneracy conventions: the statement of lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism.

proof.text: Finally all constructions are natural in the supplied diagrams. For a compatible pair $u:W\to W'$ and $v:Y\to Y'$, the equations $u_0t_{-1}=t'_{-1}v$ and $u_{n+1}t_n=t'_nu_n$ remain the very same equations after reversal. For a compatible map of homotopy diagrams $u:A\to A'$, $v:B\to B'$ with $v_{n+1}H_j^n=H_j'^nu_n$, replacing $j$ by $n-j$ gives $v_{n+1}\widetilde H_j^n=\widetilde H_j'^nu_n$. For the explicit sections, naturality of $u$ gives $u_nW(q_n)t_{-1}=W'(q_n)u_0t_{-1}=W'(q_n)t'_{-1}v$. In a parameter functor category each component is a natural transformation, and evaluation preserves its compositions and identities by definition. Thus evaluating $W\circ r^{\mathrm{op}}$, the unchanged $t_n$, the sections, or $H_{n-j}^n$ gives exactly the construction on the evaluated diagram. This proves the asserted compatibilities without a choice of pointwise homotopies.
